sentences.text: Asiaceratops was a herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaur whose name means "Asian horned face".
The type species A. salsopaludalis is found in Uzbekistan, while the second species A. sulcidens is found in China and Mongolia.
Asiaceratops salsopaludalis was formally described by Nesov, Kaznyshkina, and Cherepanov in 1989.
The specific name salsopaludalis means "of the salt marsh" in Latin.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of a fragment of a left maxilla.
In 1995, Nesov referred additional material from three Uzbek sites, including mostly skull elements and a partial humerus.
Because flowering plants were limited during the Cretaceous, Asiaceratops likely fed on ferns, cycads, and conifers.
Asiaceratops used its sharp beak to bite off leaves or needles.
Recent cladistic analyses indicate a basal position for Asiaceratops within the family Leptoceratopsidae.
More recent phylogenetic analyses consistently place Asiaceratops as a basal neoceratopsian outside the family Leptoceratopsidae.
Asiaceratops lived during the Early to Late Cretaceous periods.
Asiaceratops salsopaludalis lived in the Cenomanian stage of the mid-Cretaceous, about 99 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
The time range for Asiaceratops is the Cenomanian, spanning from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
It is debated whether Asiaceratops is a valid taxon, as it has often been considered a nomen dubium due to limited material.
